title: Part-Time Lecturer Pool, Argyros College of Business and Economics, Academic Year 2026-2027
description:
Description

The Argyros College of Business and Economics at Chapman University
invites applications for its Part-Time Lecturer pool for the
Academic year 2026-2027 in the following areas:

Accounting
Business
Economics
Entrepreneurship
Finance
Management
Marketing
Management Science
Real Estate

Appointments from the part-time pool are temporary and often made
just prior to the start of the academic term, so applicants must be
available on short notice. Fall contracts begin in mid-August and
end late-December; Spring contracts begin in mid-January and end
mid-May.  Opportunities for teaching during the Summer may also be
available.

Chapman University is a nationally-ranked institution offering
traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of
Orange County, one of Southern California’s most diverse and
vibrant regions. The University achieved R2 status in the Carnegie
Classification of Institutions of Higher Education, a distinction
held by just 10 percent of all U.S. universities and is ranked as
#100 among Best National Universities by US News and World Report
(2027). Our faculty include academic leaders who excel in research,
publishing, and world-class teaching in our 11 schools and
colleges, including the Argyros College of Business and Economics.
Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an
environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and
faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at
www.chapman.edu .

The Argyros College of Business and Economics (ACBE) is fully
accredited by AACSB and offers a variety of undergraduate and
graduate programs, including an MS in Business Analytics degree.
Chapman's full-time MBA program is ranked #53 nationally by US News
and World Report. The school currenlty has 1,800 undergraduates and
150 gradute students who attend classes in a modern 100,000 squart
foot state-of-the-art facility. Chapman is also home to the
world-renowned Economic Sciences Institute, headed by Nobel
Laureate Vernon Smith. Additional information can be found at
http://www.chapman.edu/business
.

Qualifications

Required:

1. Master's degree from an accredited institution in the subject
area being taught

2. Ability to communicate clearly and effectively orally and in
writing

3. Strong commitment to student learning, quality teaching, and
student excellence

4. Ability to teach in-person on our campus in Orange, CA

Application Instructions

Interested candidates should submit the following materials via
interfolio:

1. Curiculum Vitae

2. Names of three references with contact information

For any inquiries, pleaes contact Eva Valencia at
evalencia@chapman.edu, using " Part-Time Lecturer Pool
2026-2027 " as the email subject line.

Argyros College of Business and Economics will draw from the pool
as necessary when openings arise. Only those selected will be
contacted. Applications will remain in the pool until August 15,
2027.

Should you remain interested in future openings beyond that date,
you will need to reapply to the next academic year's posting.

The pay range for course and course related work for this position
is $52.80 per hour. This position is contingent on final budget
approval. Successful completion of a background check is required
for all selected candidates.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Chapman University is an equal opportunity employer that provides
equal employment opportunities to all individuals, regardless of
their protected characteristics. All qualified applicants and
employees are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration
for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex,
sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national
origin, ancestry, citizenship status, physical disability, mental
disability, medical condition, military and veteran status, marital
status, pregnancy, genetic information or any other characteristic
protected by state or federal law.
